subject: Next steps: procurement & hosting path options
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Gonzalez <elena@clearwavehealth.com>, Tom Reynolds <treynolds@clearwavehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Next steps: procurement & hosting path options

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a proposed path to keep procurement moving without losing momentum:

What we heard
- ClearWave will be building a real-time summarization service on clinical notes (high throughput, moderate context lengths).
- Security & procurement prefer PO-based purchases through AP (Net30 typical); corporate card is a fallback for POC buys.
- You’re evaluating SaaS marketplace routes for centralized purchasing but may also consider direct contractual engagement for committed capacity.

Options we recommend (high level)
1) Hosted (Redwood API) — fastest onboarding, usage-based billing, supports marketplace subscriptions. Good for POC and early production.
2) Dedicated Reserved — reserved GPU capacity with commit discounts and SLA options. Billed monthly via Redwood invoice (can support Net30 and PO flows).
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) — longer lead time, enterprise contract, preferred for highly regulated data or air-gapped needs.

Commercial levers to align to procurement
- Billing method: marketplace vs direct invoice (we can do both; marketplace invoices typically route through AWS/GCP marketplace invoicing team which may require different billing entity).
- Payment terms: card (immediate) vs PO/Net30 (standard for enterprise procurement).
- Commitment: on-demand vs committed monthly GPU hours (commits yield discounts and potential SLA uplift).

Attachments: pricing_summary_v2.pdf (line-item examples) and hosting_vs_dedicated_matrix.xlsx (feature/ops comparison).

Actions / ask from ClearWave
- Confirm whether procurement will accept marketplace invoices or requires Redwood to invoice directly to ClearWave (PO + Net30).
- Provide procurement contact (name + email) and any vendor onboarding docs (W-9, COI, purchasing terms).
- Indicate preferred path for an initial 3-month POC: hosted on-demand (card) or hosted with PO, or a small reserved commitment.

Proposed next step
- I can loop in our Commercial Ops (Neha) for a 30-min procurement alignment call tomorrow or Friday. Please let me know preferred time slots.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Elena Gonzalez <elena@clearwavehealth.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:16:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps: procurement & hosting path options

Thanks Marcus — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Procurement preference
- Our standard path is PO + Net30 through AP. Marketplace purchases are acceptable only if the invoice shows ClearWave as the billed customer and the marketplace supports PO numbers on their invoices. We’ll need to confirm with AP.

2) Initial procurement for POC
- We prefer starting with a PO for a 3-month runway so AP has visibility; if needed we can do a small charge on card for any expedited/eval accounts.

3) Commit vs on-demand
- For budget planning, Finance prefers an on-demand/consumption model for POC. If commits yield a substantial discount (10–20%+) we can evaluate committing mid-PO term, but primary ask is flexibility.

4) Compliance items
- Can you share SOC2 and data retention/audit log info? Also we’ll likely need a W-9 and proof of insurance.

I’m copying Tom (procurement) to provide AP contact and vendor onboarding checklist.

Best,
Elena Gonzalez
Head of AI Products | ClearWave Health
elena@clearwavehealth.com

Elena —

Great — answers below and proposed wording for procurement to speed review.

Marketplace vs direct invoicing
- We support both. Marketplace route: Redwood is the seller on AWS Marketplace (or GCP Marketplace) and invoices flow through the marketplace stack. Important note: not all marketplace invoices attach PO numbers by default — AWS has a field to include customer PO but AP teams sometimes request a vendor-side invoice showing the PO. We can provide direct invoices tied to a PO for dedicated or hosted contracts if that’s preferred.

Commit vs on-demand (pricing summary)
- On-demand (hosted): pay-per-use, no minimum, ideal for POC.
- Small commit (3-mo reserved): ~12–18% discount vs on-demand, recommended if predictable baseline usage exists.
- Large commit (12-mo reserved): ~25–35% discount + SLA uplift and priority capacity.

Docs we can share immediately
- SOC2 report (redacted) and W-9 (see links below).
- Procurement-ready purchase appendix (sample PO language) we use for Net30/PO customers.

Suggested procurement-friendly wording (copy/paste for AP)
"Redwood Inference, Inc. will provide hosted inference services under the attached Quote RW-2026-1158. Redwood will invoice ClearWave Health, Inc. per the payment terms on the Quote. Invoices will include the ClearWave PO number and are payable Net30."

Link to draft quote & docs
- Quote: https://app.redwood.ai/quotes/RW-2026-1158
- SOC2 / vendor docs: https://drive.google.com/redwood-soc2-report

Next steps
- Neha (CC) from Commercial Ops can run a short procurement alignment call to confirm invoice formatting and required attachments (W-9, COI). Neha — any availability for a 30-min call Mon or Tue next week?

Happy to join the call.

Thanks,
Marcus

Marcus / Elena —

Thanks for the clarity here. A few procurement constraints from ClearWave AP:

- We will require a W-9 and vendor legal name for our vendor onboarding — please confirm Redwood legal entity and address.
- Standard terms are Net30 on our PO; we must receive invoices that reference our PO number and contain line-item charges.
- For marketplace purchases: AP will only process via marketplace if the invoice shows ClearWave as the billed customer and includes our PO number. If marketplace routing does not support that, we need Redwood to issue a direct invoice.
- We will also need a copy of SOC2 (or a point-in-time attestation) and proof of insurance (COI).

We can start with a single PO for a 3-month POC (hosted/on-demand) and then evaluate a small commit if we hit steady-state. Please send the W-9 and a sample invoice template so our AP team has what they need.

If you can put Neha or someone from finance operations on a short call with me Monday morning (11/23) at 9:30am PT I’ll have the AP benefit from talking through the invoice layout.

Tom Reynolds
Senior Procurement Manager | ClearWave Health
treynolds@clearwavehealth.com
